papers.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
papers.problem: AI agents that forecast company earnings had no fair test against analyst forecasts.
papers.fix: Three of six models matched analyst error, but their 80% ranges held the true answer only 37-70% of the time.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you trust an AI forecast range, expect misses; widen the range before you act on it.
papers.limitation: The test covers 149 quarters from 86 US companies, so results may not hold elsewhere.

papers.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
papers.problem: Reasoning models cannot improve themselves well when only unlabeled prompts exist and no stronger teacher is available.
papers.fix: Training a model against a deliberately weakened copy of itself raised average accuracy by 4.0 to 5.5 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train small reasoning models, a squeezed copy of your own model can act as a free teacher.
papers.limitation: The gains come from math and coding tests, so other tasks may behave differently.

papers.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
papers.problem: Image generators that draw in fixed order cannot fill in or edit parts of a picture.
papers.fix: A short retraining recipe gave them fill-in skills, beating MaskGIT on inpainting (FID 6.21 versus 10.44) for 13-33% extra compute.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you already run a pretrained image model, you can add editing without training a new model from scratch.
papers.limitation: Plain image quality gets slightly worse, with class-conditional FID rising by 1.2 to 1.9.

papers.title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
papers.problem: Agent builders assumed tool protocols and command lines behave the same when they offer the same actions.
papers.fix: Identical actions scored differently through MCP and CLI; a repair step lifted all six settings by up to 9.0 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build agents, test both interfaces, because the way you show a tool changes what the agent does.
papers.limitation: The study covers six models and three environments, so other setups may differ.

papers.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
papers.problem: Developers download small quantized models from public registries, and nobody tested whether the files actually work.
papers.fix: Seven of 305 official Ollama tags (2.3%) failed code tests, and adding an importance matrix fixed three rebuilt files.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run low-bit models locally, run a quick code test first, because a valid download can still be useless.
papers.limitation: The broken files were all low-bit models with at most four billion parameters, and the screen only tested code skills.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in emerging markets set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew whether those committees change environmental results.
papers.fix: Committees link to better environmental scores, but in Islamic banks only overall scores and resource reduction improved.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you judge a bank's green claims, check its products and innovations, because a committee alone may be for show.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions show links, not cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing fast, yet nobody had mapped how they are issued or what drives their size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, they stay a tiny share, clustered in Indonesia, Malaysia and Saudi Arabia.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you want bigger green sukuk deals, use equity-based contracts and strong security, and watch second-opinion costs.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links between features and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan did not know whether AI and big data help them compete and grow sustainably.
papers.fix: AI, big data and data management link to higher competitiveness and sustainability; staff digital skill helps only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run an Islamic bank, put money into AI and data systems before staff digital training alone.
papers.limitation: It surveyed 214 managers in Jordan at one point in time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in countries with both Islamic and conventional banking did not know which digital factors drive their growth.
papers.fix: Technology adoption was the strongest growth driver across 218 banks; high-tech exports helped only alongside it.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan bank growth, build digital infrastructure first, and pair it with strong governance for Islamic banks.
papers.limitation: The data covers 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, and the study shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Muslim-majority countries still have many people outside formal finance, despite Islamic finance growing for a decade.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institutions, internet access, population and age dependency all shape financial inclusion.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you shape OIC policy, invest in digital infrastructure, youth, women and income, because OECD lessons do not copy over.
papers.limitation: The study covers only 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: What keeps gig workers motivated? A typology of the intrinsic-extrinsic motivation interplay in the digital gig economy
papers.institution: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology
papers.problem: Studies on gig workers looked at inner and outer motivation separately and ignored how digital skills affect both.
papers.fix: Gig workers describe digital skills as the link that turns mixed inner and outer motivation into steady engagement.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you freelance online, build digital skills, because they help keep you motivated and engaged.
papers.limitation: It covers only Sri Lankan platform gig workers, mostly young part-timers, at one point in time.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Researchers did not know what drives doctoral students to produce new ideas when generative AI is everywhere.
papers.fix: Inner and outer motivation both drive new ideas in chemistry doctoral students, and good resources and support cushion low motivation.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you lead a PhD lab, meet students' basic needs and supply resources, because both keep ideas coming.
papers.limitation: Single-time self-reported surveys cannot prove cause, and the reverse direction is possible.
